Kaiserliche Akademie der Geschichte - Geschichtslehrbuch Vierte Ausgabe

Frühe Geschichte und Valentia Maritima 

The history of the Hochdeutsch peoples can be traced back to the early Hochdeutsch tribes of pre-Regno Azzuro times. During this time they would create small settlements along the Stahl River and the modern-day Stahlbasin area. Archaeologists have uncovered various small scale buildings, traces of human activity as well as tools. While they seemed to have knowledge of agriculture their society was still partially nomadic with little resemblance of a centralized state or government. Religion, particularly worship of natural elements was particularly important in their society as shown by their artwork. In the north near modern day Eisenstadt there was less human activity but still some nomadic groups were found to have moved through the area. 

The history of the early Hochdeutsch, however, would be interrupted by the rise of the Imperium in the early Republican era. The early Kingdom era, middle Republican era and later Imperial era of the Regnozian Imperium is well recorded in the history of Eleysr and the world. For our purposes in discussing the history of Valentia Maritima, the Hochdeutsch province of the Imperium we will discuss the early Republican period. Following the overthrow of the corrupt King and the execution of his court the Senate of the Regnozians would be established. Based on the Greichisch polis of southern Eleysr the Senate would be a semi-democratic governing system. Made up of 127 members by 132 AD, the Senate would later be reformed to include both the lower and upper classes of society. A fusion between an aristocracy and pure democracy, the members of the Senate would be elected by the upper classes of the Regnozian society. The early Republican period, generally described as between 120 and 240 AD, would be an era of rapid expansion for the Regnozian Imperium. These would include various campaigns spanning southern Eleysr but most significantly for our purposes, conquests against the Hochdeutsch peoples. 

A series of conflicts between the Hochdeutsch tribes and the Imperium would ensue, particularly in the south of the modern day region of Stahlbasin. Evidence of this is provided in early Imperium literature as well as archaeological findings along the basin. Small scale skirmishes would continue for a decade until the campaign by Emperor Tiberius to conquer the area. The legions which far outnumbered the Hochdeutsch would place the southern Stahlbasin under Imperium control. Renamed as the province of Valentia Maritima it would serve as a valuable source of gold and iron as well as a trading hub of the Empire to the civilizations of the East. Most importantly, the Regnozians would bring large scale agriculture to the Stahlbasin. Mineral rich and fertile the basin of the Stahl River would act as the breadbasket of the Regnozian Imperium and enrich the local deputies of the area. The imperial government in the area, delegated by the Senate, would act with significant autonomy and manage local affairs without much oversight from the Imperium. To the north, the Eisenstadt and Neudresden regions would be initially independent. However, as regional trade became more and more lucrative and the Regnozians sent more military expeditions north a Foederati system would be implemented. Foedus or Foederati were cities and areas with treaties with Rome. Swearing allegiance to the Empire, they would be granted significant independence but would have to defend the Empire when called into action. The foederati city states of Eisenstadt, Ruhmstadt and Nuedresden would develop along the estuaries of the Stahl River. Collectively they would be known as the Stahl-Weser region of the Empire. 

Through Imperial power the region of the modern day Kaiserreich would remain at peace for a century with a heavily managed system of governors and Foederati being backed by the legions of the Regnozian Imperium. As the Imperium declined in the Late Imperial Period, the system holding together the Stahlbasin would begin to unravel as well. A series of unsuccessful wars with foreign powers, internal instability and a series of incompetent Emperors had slowly but surely brought the Imperium to its knees. By the time 370 AD rolled around, the capital of Parma had been sacked twice, first by the Imperiums own generals and later by the Hochdeutsch in the Foederati Coup. Marcus Novius of the Eisenstadt foederati participated in a coup in 370 AD against the heavily weakened imperial government. The Novius or Foederati coup would mark the formal end of the Regnozian Imperium as the former grand capital of the Empire burned down from eight weeks of looting and occupation. As his men looted the city Marcus Novius and the Hochdeutsch coalition army had stormed the imperial palaces on the marble hill. Inside the palace, the slaughter would be complete. The Imperial family would be massacred by the Hochdeutsch forces with Marcus Novius subsequently declaring the dissolution of the Empire, the ceding of the Stahlbasin to Eisenstadt and the formation of the Regnozian Kingdom. 

General Cornelius on the loot of Parma in 370 AD:
"Exitium Parmae, illius olim magnae urbis, completum erat. Ego et mei viri nunc per vias urbis vacuae et exustae ambulamus, umbra eius quod fuit. Aulae illius magni Imperii, quod Eleysr pervagabatur, nunc desertae et deiectae iacent. Defensores urbis aut a Hochdeutsch interfecti sunt aut arma posuerunt atque ad Ravennam in meridie fugerunt. Viri ex Eisenstadt, Ruhmstadt atque etiam ex Stahl nunc urbem vagantur, caedem et direptionem facientes."
Dissolution of Imperial Power and Civil War

Introduction

Marcus Novius had envisioned a grand empire for Eisenstadt when he had couped the Imperial government in Parma but that would not be the case. His actions had let loose a century of civil war and destruction where the Hochdeutsch people would become more fractured than ever before. Initially, the coup of Parma would be seen as an Eisenstadt victory but the reality on the ground would quickly prove differently. Marcus Novius tenuous claim on the Stahlbasin would be broken as the area splintered in various rival factions and warlords out of his control. Generals of the former Regnozian legions would establish their own feudal states across the southern Stahlbasin with Imperial authority now removed. A series of wars between rival factions of the Regnozian elite in the Stahlbasin would leave them weakened. 

The united Hochdeutsch Confederation composed of the northern Stahl River city-states would sweep in and take control of the region. During this era, the Hochdeutsch Confederation would carry out a removal of remaining Regnozian elements in society. The remaining groups of Regnozians would be hunted down by the Hochdeutsch military and removed. By the thousands the Regnozians would be killed, their properties taken away and their buildings destroyed. The mass expulsion and slaughter of the Regnozians would reduce their population from 4.5 million in 392 to 210,000 by 397 AD. Today, the influence of the Regnozians is still seen in the southern Stahl River region where small minority Regnozian communities still live. However, the peace between the north Stahl River city-states through the confederation would be short-lived. The dissolution of the Confederation in 415 following the exit of Ruhmstadt and Stahlbasin in protest of Eisenstadts domination of the alliance would lead to several decades of war. Termed the seven decade war, the Stahl city-states would fight among themselves in a changing web of alliances. 

Seven Decade War

The Hochdeutsch Confederation, an organization of northern city-states including Eisenstadt, Ruhmstadt, Neudresden and eventually Stahlbasin would dissolve in 415 AD. Following the Regnozian expulsion and the rise of Eisenstadt's military power, the city of Eisenstadt had begun to demand tribute from other Confederation city-states in return for protection. The situation would come to a head in 415 when Ruhmstadt and Stahlbasin refused to pay tribute and left the Confederation. Its full dissolution would come later in the year as Stahlbasin fell out of Confederation control and declared itself the Kingdom of Stahl. In response, the Kingdom of Eisenstadt would begin a ruthless military campaign against the other northern city-states. Marching on Ruhmstadt in 417 AD, Otto Schneider would siege the city of Ruhmstadt. Following six months of siege, the city of Ruhmstadt would surrender as its population began to starve and the outer city walls were overrun by the Eisenstadt army. Subsequently, the triumphant Eisenstadt army would loot the city of Ruhmstadt, burning down dozens of Regnozian-era Churches and palaces as well as taking anything of value. The following spring, the Eisenstadt army would be on the move again. Their march towards Neudresden, however, would be cut short by the death of Schneider V who would drown in the crossing of the River Stahl. 

In 432 AD, his successor Felix Schneider I would declare war on Neudresden. After defeating the Neudresdent militia forces in the battle of Dunkelberg he would lay siege to the city. The Regnozian walls, the largest in northern Eleysr at the time would prove particularly difficult to break. The three layers of defenses; an outer wall, a secondary wall and a citadel would slow the Eisenstadt advance. Constant bombardment of the walls using trebuchets didnt seem to create so much as a dent on the old city walls. Realizing the war wouldnt end quickly, the Eisenstadt forces would dig in for a long siege to starve out their opponents. Inside, the city of Neudresden would be well provisioned with a significant grain supply being held within the citadel. Neudresdens allies from the south would attempt to break the Eisenstadt supply lines and thus break the siege. Attacks on the supply lines from Eisenstadt to the besieging army as well as sabotage would prove to be a significant problem for the siege campaign. An inconsistent supply of food, men and weapons to sustain the siege would eventually lead to Kaiser Felix Schneider to call off the campaign in 434 and return to Eisenstadt empty-handed. 

Defeat, however, would not be final. In 440, Eisenstadt would return to Neudresden in the Spring to lay siege yet again. Powerful new trebuchets and the aid of mercenaries would allow them to break through the first outer wall by the second month of the siege. Learning the lesson of supply lines, the Kaiser realized he would have to end the siege quickly. Although he suffered significant casualties he would be able to break the citadel by the third month of siege through tunnel warfare. Eisenstadt retaliation for their previous losses would be swift and brutal. Thousands of residents of Neudresden would be slaughtered in the coming days during the military occupation. Once the two cities were brought back into the fold, the Kaiser would declare the establishment of the Northern Hochdeutsch Empire. Within the hall of the Neudresden citadel the Kaiser would proclaim the establishment of the Empire with Eisenstadt at the helm. 

From 442 to 447 AD Kaiser Felix Schneider would be the first to hold the title King of the Hochdeutsch. Eventually when he died a succession crisis would break out amongst his sons. The Empire would be divided into separate Kingdoms including the Kingdom of Ruhmstadt, the Kingdom of Eisenstadt and the Duchy of Neudresden which would be united through a military alliance. The Kingdom of Eisenstadt would begin another war against Stahlbasin to bring it back into the hold of the northern city-states. With the aid of House Sturmfels, the Kaiser of Eisenstadt would be able to quickly crush the ineffective Kingdom of Stahlbasin. In return, the Kaiser would grant House Sturmfels the title of Lords of Stahlbasin and give them feudal privileges over the region. Following the annexation of Stahlbasin the area that encompasses modern-day western Kaiserreich would remain in relative peace until 550 AD. During this time a succession crisis between the two brothers of the late King of Ruhmstadt would break into an all out regional war as Eisenstadt and Neudresden would back different successors. To cut out Eisenstadt, a massive Neudresden army of 110,000 men would march on the city. Arriving as reinforcement the Lords of Stahlbasin would arrive in the city, depose the Kaiser and declare themselves the King of the Hochdeutsch. To maintain a tenuous peace with Neudresden and the House Braun they would accept the Neudresden backed successor of Ruhmstadt and allow Neudresden autonomy from the former military alliance system. 

In 560 AD, the Erseter Kaiser of the Hochdeutsch Empire would declare war on House Braun and the city of Neudresden. With Ruhmstadt remaining neutral, the Erster Kaiser would quickly crush Neudresden. To maintain House Sturmfels hegemony he would marry his first born son into House Braun to maintain an alliance. With the Hochdeutsch people being united under one dynasty for the first time in centuries, the era of civil war would be over. 

Early Imperial Era

Establishment of the Kaiserliche Kriegskult 

The uniting of the Hochdeutsch people for the first time in centuries, this time under a Hochdeutsch ruler and not a Regnozian would be a momentous occasion in the history of the Kaiserreich. The Erster Kaiser who had brought an end to the chaos of constant civil war, looting and destruction would be venerated and deified by the Kaiserliche Kriegskult or Imperial War Cult. Following his death in 573 AD, the Erster Kaiser would be deified and become the leading figure in the pantheon of Gods held by the Kaiserliche Kriegskult. With the support of the Kaisers successors the Kriegskult would become the state-enforced religion of the Hochdeutsch. The pagan faiths of the Regnozians and the traditions of naturalism that had survived would be purged during this time and forced to make way for the new state religion. 

The holy text of the Kriegskult, the Das Buch von Stahl und Eisen, would set forth several central doctrines of the Kriegskult. First, the Erster Kaiser would be seen as a higher deity who had come down from a higher realm to unify the great Hochdeutsch peoples. Second, the Kaisers of his lineage would be his future representatives and were granted the divine right to rule. Lastly, the Hochdeutsch peoples have the divine destiny to rule over the world and bring it under Hochdeutsch hegemony. In it the Kriegskult describes a constant struggle between chaos and order with the Kaisers being the representatives of order and enemies of the state being unholy agents of chaos. 
Das Buch von Stahl und Eisen, 1:4:32
"Ordo naturalis, status ordinis, imperat Kaiser omnipotentem ex progenie primi Kaiser. Qui sunt inimici civitatis, inimici sunt gentis Hochdeutsch. Hi sunt actores chaos, qui contra divinitus decretum fatum gentis Hochdeutsch operantur."
The natural order, the state of order, demands an all powerful Kaiser from the first Kaisers lineage. Those who are enemies of the state, are enemies of the Hochdeutsch peoples. They are actors of chaos who work against the divinely-ordained destiny of the Hochdeutsch peoples. 

The Golden Age of the Early Imperial Period

The Golden Age of the First Imperial Period set forth by the Erster Kaiser would last from 573 to 760 AD. During the roughly two centuries that encompassed the golden age a strong state and consistent stability would allow the expansion and growth of the Kaiserreich. Internally, the Hochdeutsch Empire went into an era of massive economic and population growth. Massive infrastructure projects including the Kaiserliche Kanal would boost interregional trade. The Kaiserliche Kanal or Imperial Canal in particular would connect the southern breadbasket of the Stahlbasin and the manufacturing cities of the north. Taking seventeen years to complete and thousands of peasant laborers, the Kanal would act as a hydraulic highway that allowed merchants, armies and citizens to transit quickly. Cities along the route including Dunkelberg, Eisenstadt and Stahlbasin would boom into trade centers that would deal in everything from finished products to grain, beer and wool. On top of this a centralized state would allow the revamping of the imperial road system which had long been neglected and destroyed during the centuries of civil war. A grand highway would be built connecting the capital of Stahlbasin and the northern cities. Successive Kaisers would also reform the imperial bureaucracy to include an examination system as well as establishing a public schooling system. 

Most importantly, the Kaiser would reform the Kaiserliche Armee. Instead of having city-states running their own militias the Kaisers would centralize the military under an imperial state. On top of this, instead of allowing families to succeed each other in the military, the Kaisers would impose an examination system for recruiting applicants into the Kaiserliche Armee. Another key piece of the Kaiserliche Armee would be its cavalry which would become one of the most effective in northern Eleysr through their emphasis on speed and maneuverability. During this era militarism would become pervasive through society with all members of society being expected to contribute to war efforts. 

First Qashliq-Hochdeutsch War

As the Hochdeutsch stabilized internally they began to turn their attention outside of the Empire. Towards interior Eleysr which was rich in resources the newly established Kaiserliche Armee would face their first test. The Qashliq Khanat which had remained the rulers of the area since they pushed out the Regnozian Imperium had ruled for centuries. In 620 AD, the Kaiserliche Armee led by General Konrad Mayer would cross the River Nördlich into Khanate territory. Driving towards the Khanates capital of Qashliq the General would arrive in its outskirts within three weeks of march. Through a constant artillery bombardment the Hochdeutsch forces would crush the entrenched Qashliq forces and drive them out of the area. The General would pursue the Qashliq forces and the Khan further north to the reaches of the Ob steppes while leaving his subordinates to hold the city. As he and the Kaiserliche Armee marched north he would be ambushed by the Qashliq horde at the Battle of the Ob River. When the Kaiserliche Armee was attempting to cross the frigid river at a passing located in a valley they would be surrounded and attacked by the Khanate forces. Attempting to execute a fighting retreat the General would order his forces to cross to the eastern bank of the river. While attempting to swim across he would drown under the weight of his own chain mail. With leadership being removed the remaining forces were cut down by the Khanate. 

When news arrived to the occupying Fifth Armee in Qashliq of the Generals demise his subordinates would quickly burn down the city and retreat back across the Nördlich. Before leaving the city they would massacre its residents, loot its valuables and execute a fighting retreat back into Kaiserreich territory. Choosing not to pursue into Kaiserreich territory the Khan would remain on the eastern bank of the Nördlich. The disastrous outcome of the First Qashliq-Hochdeutsch war would lead to the Kaiser purging all commanders related to the military disaster. 

Second Qashliq-Hochdeutsch War

In 632 AD, to restore the honor of the Kaiserreich the Kaiser ordered another military campaign against the Khanate. First, they would move south to cut off the vassals of the Khan, defeating the Manstyi at the Battle of Irman and subjugating them. Then crossing the River Nördlich again, they would defeat the Khan in August of 634 at the Battle of the River Nördlich through use of superior artillery and maneuvering tactics by the Kaiserliche cavalry. As the Khanate horde pulled back from the River the Kasierreich cavalry corps would quickly flank and surround them. Slow moving foot soldiers would then follow and deliver the final blow to the Khan. Around 27,000 Khanate soldiers and 15,000 Kasierliche Armee forces would be killed during the battle, wiping out the majority of the Khans fighting forces. When the sons of the Khan attempted to proclaim the continuation of the Khanate, the Kaiserliche Armee would march on Qashliq one last time. Upon reaching the city the Armee proceeded to quickly crush the remaining weakened Qashliq Khanate forces and kill the successors of the Khan in their own palace. 

Settlement of Östliche Provinzen

Upon the deposition of the Khanate, the Imperial Government in Neudresden would proclaim the new imperial province of Ostliche Provinzen or the Eastern Province. A series of expeditions into the area by imperial cartographers would map out the area for further expansion, settlement and exploitation of local resources. By the thousands the citizens of the Kaiserreich would move into the Eastern Province and displacing the local population of Qashliq. Incidents of violence between the settlers and the native Qashliq would become common-place as the two groups disputed over land and resources. The doctrine of the Kriegskult proclaimed that the Ostliche Provinzen was divinely mandated to the Hochdeutsch people and its settlement was integral to the greatness of the Hochdeutsch people. The Kaiser, an extreme expansionist, would strongly support settlement efforts into the northeast. It was proclaimed that any male citizen of the Reich over twenty years of age would be granted free land in the east if he was able to properly settle the area. An initial fifty acres would be given for free and an extra twenty would be given for every family member he brought with him. A series of conflicts between the native Qashliq and the Hochdeutsch would flare up in the eastern reaches of the Ostliche Provinzen. Following a skirmish that killed twenty Hochdeutsch settlers, the Kaiserliche Armee would be called forth by the Kaiser. The mandate would be to remove or kill every Qashliq in the entirety of the Empire for they stood in front of the divine mandate given by the Erster Kaiser. During this time the Kaiserliche Armee would carry out massive atrocities against the native population. Eventually of the eighteen million Qashliq, eleven million would be removed from the Empire and expelled to the north. Two million would be killed by the Kaiserliche Armee with the Kaiserreich additionally cutting off food supplies to majority Qashliq areas. The remaining Qashliq would be rounded up by the settlers and Kaiserliche Armee and placed on Indianerreservates in the far rural reaches of the province. 

Erster Südenkrieg

The Erster Südenkrieg or First Southern War was a series of unsuccessful military campaigns between the Kaiserreich and the lowland or tiefland nations to the south. As settlers moved to the Ostliche Provinzen the Kaiserliche Armee high command or Kriegskommand would turn its eyes southwards. During the collapse of the Regnozain Imperium portions of Valentia Maritima would break off from the central Stahlbasin authorities and form a confederation of city-states and petty kingdoms. They would remain largely untouched during the civil war between the Hochdeutsch as military campaigns turned inwards between the city-states of the north. However, as the centralized state restrengthened it turned its eyes to reuniting itself with the Tiefland. 

By the 750s, nearing the end of the Early Imperial Era, the major lowland nations were composed of Vandermere, Brennsland, Ostmere and Fensbruck. Vandermere and Ostmere bordered the westernmost portions of Ostliche Provinzen and were susceptible to an initial Kaiserliche Armee assault. Overnight in August of 753 the Kaiser ordered the 3rd and 2nd Kaiserliche Armee units to cross into Vandermere territory. The vastly outnumbered Vandermere, he assumed, would fall quickly. The armies stormed the capital city within hours and occupied the area. However, the occupation effort would be greatly damaged by the constant sabotage and elusive rebels in the rural areas of Vandermere. When a coalition of Tiefland nations composed of Ostmere, Brennsland and Vandermere rebels formed to oust the Kaiserreich the Kaiserliche Armee would pull out of Vandermere. 

In 757 AD, the Kaiserreich returned to Tiefland. This time they resorted to scorched earth tactics to subjugate the Vandermere peoples. The Kriegskommand would contribute significant resources to combating rebels and any Vandermere citizens suspected of aiding anti-Kaiserreich causes would be put to death. Most of the population through the course of half a decade would be relocated to Sicherheitszones or safe zones which were heavily fortified and regulated urban areas which Kaiserliche Armee officers controlled. During this time the Vandermere would be a military governed zone under martial law where Generals were given total command to do what they wished to defeat the rebels. By 773 the area was determined to be pacified and was then fully annexed into the Kaiserreich. 

Zweite Südenkrieg

The Zweite Südenkrieg would come in 789 AD. Following the subjugation of Vandermere, the Kriegskommand had established an alliance with the Tiefland nation of Fennsbruck. However, when King Elsje de Bruin died in 788, his son, would terminate the alliance with the Kaiserreich on the grounds of preventing further expansionism into the Tiefland. The second Armee would be dispatched to the border between Vandermere and Fennsbruck, armed with newly acquired artillery. The cannons, armed with gunpowder from the oriental east, would be used to pound Fennsbruck with continuous artillery fire. For seven days the barrage would continue with cannonballs flying across the border into the Fennsbruckian capital. In the end the city would be laid to waste and the Kaiserliche Armee would pull back, determining that the cost of occupation would be too great. From 789 to the early 1900s the Tiefland would remain largely independent of the Kaiserreich.

Industrialization 

From an Agrarian to an Industrial Society

Up until the 1850s the Technokratisches economy would remain largely agrarian with the majority of economic activity being produced in the Stahlbasin region. Stahlbasin which was the breadbasket of the nation produced massive quantities of grain and corn which fueled the nation. However, in the 1860s this began to change as the industrial revolution began in the Kaiserreich. The invention of the steam engine and the factory line in Eisenstadt would rapidly transform the nation by bringing the railroad, mass production and automobiles to the nation. Massive factories began to spring up across the nation, particularly in the northern cities of Eisenstadt, Ruhmstadt and Neudresden which led to an influx of residents. In particular the city of Eisenstadt which was located along the Stahl River would become a center of mills and steel production. 

The industrialization of the nation would have several profound effects on the economy, society and the military. A new oligarch class would slowly replace the old feudal aristocracy, a new elite built on industrial production and the exploitation of these newfound inventions to produce profound levels of wealth. These oligarchs included industrialists such as Hendrik Veldkamp, Friedrich Weber and Johann Richter. Hendrik Velkamp, from the region of Vandermere moved to the Stahlbasin and began the company Stahlwerke AG which initially began as a steel producer and would later expand into a multi-industry conglomerate. Friedrich Weber, the father of the factory line, perfected the process of an assembly line which he used to produce petroleum automobiles while Johnann Richter possessed a monopoly on the oil produced in the nation as well as its overseas holdings. Together, these three men possessed the same amount of power and if not more over the Kaiserreich. Their tremendous wealth would allow them to sway the government and the greater society. Fearing their increasing control, the Kaiser would break up their monopolies in the 1890s breaking their control. 

In the cities the stratification of society from industrialization became all too clear. The wealthy oligarchs in the Woodhaven district of Eisenstadt in their mansions could be seen in the lower slums. Massive influxes of peasants seeking opportunities in cities had generated a new class: the urban poor. Critical but despised they worked the factory jobs across the meatpacking, automobile and steel production industries. Crime would become rampant in the cities as almost nonexistent policing would struggle to overcome the surge in illicit activity. The creation of the urban poor would also create a base for communism which would become a problem for the incumbent Kaiserreich government later on. The military began to adapt the industrial revolution for their purposes as well. Industrialized warfare would increase the lethality of the Kaiserliche Armee tenfold. Chemical weapons, mass produced rifles, machine guns, explosives and industrial artillery would all become available to the imperial arsenal. As the remaining Tiefland nations kept their feudal era militaries the Kaiserliche Armee would leap into the industrial age of warfare. 

Rise of Communism

In the second of March 1910 a Hochdeutsch man called Otter Keller in Ruhmstadt would complete the first copy of Das gemeinschaftliche Leben und die Übel des Kapitalismus or more simply put; Ubel des Kapital. In it were a series of grievances against the capitalist class created by the industrial revolution or as he put it: the oligarchs. On top of this the text criticized what it believed to be the inherent destruction of capitalism and the Kaiserliche system which he said was responsible for the stratification and war prominent in society. When the text was distributed by the thousands across the Kaiserreich it would resonate the most with the urban poor who had been left behind. Their daily struggles with factory work, low wages and corrupt authorities would be resonated in the writing of Otto Keller. The imperial government would attempt to suppress the distribution of the work but widespread printing presses had prevented significant progress. As government agents began to follow Otto Keller he would flee to Fennsbruck in 1914, barely escaping the authorities. However, when Otto Keller escaped the police would begin to round up suspected communists across the cities. Oftentimes, particularly in Ruhmstadt, communism would be violently oppressed by the imperial government which viewed it as a threat to the social cohesion of the Hochdeutsch peoples. After a riot in the slums of Ruhmstadt the Kaiser would declare any communist political activity, gatherings, and writings to be illegal. 

Kolonialism

In 1783, a Hochdeutsch explorer by the name of Felix Richter would discover a series of islands in the southern oceans. Sent by the Royal Spice Company of Eisenstadt his task was to look for peoples and lands possessing immensely valuable spice. Upon arriving on the central island he noted that there was the perfect environment for the production of pepper and nutmeg. After negotiating with the local tribes the Kaiserreich would be allowed to establish a port on the main island for the purpose of buying and exporting the spices back to Eleysr. The trade relationship would remain mutually beneficial until 1903 when the industrial revolution had begun to create a massive demand for iron. When company surveyors found significant iron deposits in the Eisenarchipel pressure came upon the Kaiser to seize the land for the Kaiserreich. Particularly from the owners of Stahlwerke, the most valuable and productive business in the reich there would be significant lobbying efforts. 

Personally the Kaiser held doubts about colonial efforts in the Eisenarchipel. He had fought in the southern Eleysr wars where he had seen hundreds of Hochdeutsch casualties as they struggled against irregular native forces on the island. It seems to me that any invasion of the faraway Eisenarchipel will become a slog, he remarked privately to members of the Kriegskommand. Nevertheless at the behest of the Kriegskommands members, the Reichswehr began to draft plans for a subjugation of the Eisenarchipel should the time come. The seventh fleet with Kriegsmarine forces would land on the central island using the existing port as a beachhead and push inwards according to Generalplan Eisenarchipel. After the central island was taken under Hochdeutsch control they would be able to reign in the remaining islanders. The plans to annex the Eisenarchipel would remain undisclosed for several years. The catalyst for the war is widely disputed by historical scholars. Some claim that the supposed attack on the port by the natives was a false flag operation carried out by members of the seventh fleet under orders from the Kreigskommand. Others believe that foreign interference had prompted the natives to attack the Kaiserliche port. However, no matter the motivation, an attack by unknown individuals would be mounted on the southern port held by the Kaiserreich. Outrage at the attack poured out across the Empire and the Kaiser acted quickly to address it. Operation Eisenarchipel would be approved. 

The Seventh Fleet on patrol in the southern oceans moved quickly to support the port. Naval guns slammed the main island for days softening the native resistance to a landing force. Shells from the naval guns arced over the skies to burn enemies miles away. Finally, as the smoke cleared from the island the Kaiserliche Marine and Kriegsmarine began to land forces into the port.
